questions.question: A ray of light is incident on the pole of a concave mirror. The acute angle between the incident ray and the principal axis will be called:
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **acute angle** between the **incident ray** and the **principal axis** is called the **angle of incidence.**
 
• **Angle of incidence** is the angle between the **incident ray** and the** normal** to the surface at the point of incidence.
 
• **Angle of emergence** is the angle between the** emergent ray** and the** normal **to the surface at the point of emergence.
 
• **Angle of reflection** is the angle between the** reflected ray** and the** normal** to the surface at the point of incidence.
 
• **Angle of deviation** is the angle between the **incident ray** and the **emergent ray.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A **concave mirror** is a **curved mirror** in which the **inner side **of the curved shape is the **reflecting surface.**
 
• Its surface has an **inward curvature** that makes it resemble the interior surface of a **hollow sphere.**
 
• Because concave mirrors enable **light beams** to converge or come together after reflection, they are also known as** converging mirrors.**

questions.question: If a coil of a conductor with 50 Ω resistance is subjected to time varying magnetic field such that the EMF induced is 5 V, then the induced current in the coil is:
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **induced current **in the coil is given by **Ohm's law,** which states that** I = V/R, **where V is the induced EMF and R is the resistance of the coil.
 
• Thus, the induced current in the coil is** 5/50 = 0.1 A.**
 
• The **direction** of the induced current is determined by **Lenz's law,** which states that the direction of the induced current is such that it** opposes **the **change in magnetic flux **that caused it.
 
• In this case, the **time varying magnetic field** is inducing an** EMF **in the coil, so the induced current will flow in a direction that** creates a magnetic field** that opposes the original magnetic field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• When a **magnetic field** passes through the coil, it induces an **EMF in the coil**, which can cause a** current to flow** if the coil is connected to a circuit.
 
• The** resistance **of the coil is a measure of how much the** coil resists the flow of current **through it.
 
• It depends on the **material of the wire, **the **length and cross-sectional area** of the wire, and the **temperature **of the wire.

questions.question: Find the cost of fencing of a rectangular land, if it has an area of 100 m² and one side of length 20 m at a rate of ₹30 per meter.
questions.solution:
Given:

The cost of fencing = Rs. 30/m2

The area of rectangle = Rs. 100 m²

The length of the rectangular = 20 m

Formula used:

Area of a rectangle = l × b

Perimeter of rectangle = 2 (l + b)

l = Length of the rectangle

b = Breadth of the rectangle

Calculation:

20 × b = 100

⇒ b = 5

The perimeter of the rectangular garden = 2 (20 + 5) = 2 × 25 = 50 m

The cost of fencing = Rs. 30/metre

∴ Total cost of fencing = 50 × 30 = Rs. 1500

**The answer is 1500.**
